name: The Decision Box Gallery
description: Find one figure in a crowded masterpiece, live on Decision 3

paragraphs: Find one figure in a crowded masterpiece with Box questions on Decision 3 (d3 and d3-flash), the decision models of vLLM Semantic Router, live on the free Decision API at decision.vllm-sr.ai. Every search, the presets included, is a live request from your browser: nothing is precomputed.
The staged search. A whole painting read at once is read small, and one figure in a crowd is a few pixels. So every search runs in four steps, each one a real request:
show the figure? One more asks it of the whole work at once, for a figure larger than a tile. If no tile and not the whole work shows it, the search ends here with "Not found".
features: Tiles. The work is cut into tiles, each read at full resolution, with one yes / no question per tile: does it
Zoom. The most likely tile is enlarged by a quarter on every side.
Box. One Box question on that tile; the API answers it with 65 yes / no sub-questions on a zooming grid, and the
Edge checks. Four yes / no questions in one request: is the figure cut off by the top, bottom, left or right
Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Netherlandish Proverbs (1559), Gemäldegalerie, Berlin
